The home mountain of the Greek Gods is Mount Olympus.

To understand the concept of search engines using the provided analogy, imagine the Internet as a massive, chaotic library that never stops growing. In this library, every website is a unique book, and every individual web page is a single page within that book. If you were looking for a specific fact, finding it in a physical library would require a card catalog or index to tell you exactly which shelf and which page to check. Without this index, you would have to read every single book from cover to cover, which is impossible. Search engines like Google act as this intelligent index. They do not just list books; they scan the contents of every page and create a detailed map. When you ask a question, the search engine uses this map to instantly point you to the exact "book" (website) and "page" (web page) that contains the answer, saving you from having to search through the entire library manually.
